research_question: How should one event be rendered differently for hearing and touch, then recombined as a coherent percept?

synthesis.engineering_hypothesis: Do not send the audio mix unchanged to body transducers. Derive a tactile mix whose encoding prioritizes temporal structure, contact mechanics, and receptor recruitment.
synthesis.system_model: event -> auditory renderer + tactile renderer -> cross-modal temporal alignment -> unified percept

findings.claim: Tactile pitch judgments can follow temporal periodicity even when the corresponding fundamental component is absent.
findings.implication: Envelope periodicity may be a stronger tactile carrier than fine spectral detail.

findings.claim: Touch can discriminate multiple temporal and spectral timbre features, with particular strength for temporal structure.
findings.implication: Encode attack time and amplitude modulation explicitly in a tactile renderer.

findings.claim: A fingertip rendering of speech-envelope timing can alter activity in auditory speech-processing regions during speech-in-noise tasks.
findings.implication: Auditory cortex may integrate temporally structured information delivered through touch.

findings.claim: Perceived tactile intensity may track the spatial population of recruited afferents better than only the local peak beneath an actuator.
findings.implication: Actuator spacing, preload, contact material, anatomy, and mechanical coupling belong in the signal model.

findings.claim: Low-frequency physiological responses depend on interactions among frequency, acoustic field, phase, duration, and body geometry rather than a simple one-frequency/one-effect map.
findings.implication: Reject isolated magic-frequency claims; log the complete physical exposure geometry.

findings.claim: An experimental audio-to-haptic pipeline used both acoustic and semantic information to choose tactile output.
findings.implication: Meaning can become an input to a tactile rendering policy rather than remaining outside the signal path.

design_constraints: Preserve raw audio and derived tactile features as separate data streams.
Timestamp every modality against one monotonic clock.
Record actuator, mounting, preload, body site, posture, and room geometry.
Treat subjective and physiological outcomes as measurements, not promised effects.
Keep experimental output amplitude inside independently established hardware and human-safety limits.
